steps.path: A conversation, after the assistant proposes a plan; the Specialists button; Settings → Specialists
steps.headline: This is what done means for plans.

rows.statement: The assistant can offer a plan on any cloud model and on local models from the 9B class up, never smaller.
Progress shows on the plan card itself: each step ticks off and its specialists sit inside it.
A plan that hits its limit pauses in place: finished work stays, the stuck step says why, and Add budget and Stop are offered.
One card shows the whole plan before anything is spent: the steps, who does them, the limit, Approve and Comment.
A model with no published price shows the limit as an amount of work only, never a made-up dollar figure.
Comment opens a note box under the plan; the assistant rewrites the plan and posts a new card.
A plan under your limit starts on its own and says so on the card, with the limit still printed.
Add budget asks for one number, shows what it is worth in dollars, and continues from where the plan stopped.
rows.note: out of curiosity, does pausing/resuming after credit limit is reached itself consume tokens? or is it no-cost pause/resume?

rows.statement: After a restart the card returns as interrupted, showing the steps already done, and nothing runs until you press Continue.
rows.note: move buttons to right side. also, stop should be to the left of the whie button on this and the previous card.

rows.statement: A finished plan folds to its step list and one line: how long it took and what it used.
After a Comment the old plan greys out and points to the new one below it.
Settings has a Plans section with 'Run small plans without asking', off by default, showing the limit once on.
While the plan is being written the card is exactly one row tall, like every other collapsed card.
Each step is its own bordered container with its specialists inside it, so plan, step and specialist read by shape.
The Add budget field reads 'Allow 9,000 tokens ($0.03)', with no extra words like 'more' or 'about'.
rows.note: same as before, maybe put warning+buttons in container together?

rows.statement: The paused plan's sentence and its buttons sit together in one filled, outlined amber pill.
Raising the limit happens inside that same amber pill, with the reason for the pause still readable beside it.
An interrupted plan gets the same pill, filled and outlined in neutral grey.
Each specialist inside a plan is the usual specialist card you can open to see its thinking, output and tool calls.
rows.note: i want to keep our current agent/specialist cards that show thinking, output, and tool calls  for agents within the plan. this should have a clear visual heirarchy of collapsed cards (Plan->Step->Specialist). stop the plan should also have the red theming used for other stop buttons in the ui and sit at the bottom right, not the left

rows.statement: Stop the plan uses the app's red stop styling and sits at the right of the card, not the left.
The paused message no longer says 'Nothing is spent past the limit you approved', and its Stop is tinted red.
rows.note: drop "nothing is spent past limit you approved. move the add budget/stop buttons to bottom right. make stop red-tint like earlier suggestions

rows.statement: Wherever a filled and a light button sit together, the light one is on the left and the filled one on the right.
rows.note: okay. the approve button should be on the rightmost side, with comment to the left of it. again, our design/style guidelines should note something to the effect of "when using FILLED/DARK buttons, these should always be either centered and the full width of the card/modal they are attached to or on the righthand side. they should never be left-aligned. when a dark and hollow/light button are placed together, the light button always goes on the left.

rows.statement: Approve sits at the right edge of a proposed plan, with Comment just to its left.
rows.note: we can put the buttons in-line with the text on the left. lots of empty space.

rows.statement: Approve and Comment sit on the same line as the limit text, and drop below it on a narrow window.
An approximate limit shows a ~ before the number ('Up to ~42,000 tokens'), with no extra warning sentence.
An approximate dollar amount also uses the ~ ('~$0.12'), never 'about $0.12'.
A failed plan says what went wrong in one line, with Report bug and Diagnose buttons.
A specialist stopped before it did anything reads 'Not started', muted, with an empty circle.
When a plan's specialist asks you something, the bottom bar's Specialists button shows '1 needs you'.
Clicking that button shows the waiting plan specialist with its question, Yes and No, Note and Stop.
A specialist waiting on your answer, in a plan or not, turns its conversation's dot red.
A specialist waiting on your answer also plays the app's alert sound, as the assistant's own questions do.
rows.threshold: the sound plays in a dev instance

rows.statement: The Specialists button also counts a plan's specialists while they are simply working, grouped under their plan.
rows.note: but we need to associate each one with it's plan. maybe we group them with plan card within the specialists chip? idk...

rows.statement: The Specialists popup lists each running plan once, saying where it is, such as 'step 1 of 3', like its card.
In that popup a plan is a 'Plan: …' card as wide as other specialists, with no separate heading, opening onto its specialists.
No 'Note for the assistant' row appears in the chat below a plan card.
A paused plan never hands itself to the assistant; it shows 'Ask the assistant' as the light button on the left.
After you ask, the card greys out and says the assistant is looking now, or will after its current reply.
The chat shows 'You asked the assistant about this plan.' after you ask.
If the assistant can't answer, the card gives the real reason with Retry, and its normal buttons come back.
On a narrow window, step titles wrap and a paused plan's buttons move below its reason, all readable.
A plan paused for a reason other than its limit offers Stop and Continue instead of Add budget.
rows.note: but auto recover where that makes the most sense and we dont actually need user input

rows.statement: On the phone, a plan card's buttons are disabled with the note 'Plans aren't available on the phone yet.'
rows.note: this will be planned. eventually, everything supported on desktop should work on mobile.

rows.statement: A plan button pressed while the app is still starting says 'The assistant isn't available right now.' with Retry.
At phone width a step's usage text wraps or shortens, and is never cut off at the screen edge.
Limits read '9,000-token limit', never '9,000 tokens limit', in step details and the spending line.
